description: Turns the notes, wheels and clock of a MIDI device into control voltages

outputs.text: The pitch of the note being played, a volt per octave with middle C at 0V; the pitch bend wheel is added to it
10V while a note is held and 0V once it is released
The velocity of the note played, 0V to 10V across MIDI velocity 0 to 127
Channel pressure from the MIDI device, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127
The position of the pitch bend wheel, -5V to +5V, resting at 0V
The position of the mod wheel, 0V to 10V across MIDI values 0 to 127
A 1ms 10V pulse each time a note is pressed, so an envelope can be restarted during a held phrase
A 1ms 10V pulse on every MIDI clock tick, which is 24 ticks to the quarter note
A 1ms 10V pulse on one MIDI clock tick in every 24, giving a pulse per quarter note; the menu offers divisions from a whole note to every tick
A 1ms 10V pulse when the MIDI device sends a start message
A 1ms 10V pulse when the MIDI device sends a stop message
A 1ms 10V pulse when the MIDI device sends a continue message

notes: nothing comes out until a MIDI device is chosen; a new one comes up with no device, and its channel line reads All channels
the driver, device and channel are picked by left-clicking the three lines of the display, each of which opens a menu of its own; none of them is on the panel's right-click menu
menu: Polyphony channels — how many notes sound at once, Monophonic or 2 to 16, which is also how many channels the note outputs carry
Monophonic priority — which held note is played while Polyphony channels is Monophonic: Last, First, Lowest or Highest
Polyphony allocation — which channel a new note is given: Rotate, Reuse, Reset or MPE
Retrigger on legato release — sends an RTRG pulse when the note being played is released and another held note takes over, while Polyphony channels is Monophonic
Use release velocity — makes VEL carry the velocity of the note off message once a note is let go
Pitch bend range — how far the wheel bends V/OCT: Off, 1 to 11 semitones, or 1, 2, 3 or 4 octaves
Smooth pitch/mod wheel — slews the PW and MW outputs towards each new value instead of stepping to it
CLK/N divider — what one pulse at CLK/N stands for: Whole, Half, Quarter, 8th, 16th, 32nd, 12 PPQN or 24 PPQN
Reset MIDI (Panic) — drops every held note and returns the outputs to rest
